questions.q: What is the real advantage of a reusable mask function like mask_ssn over per-table masking logic?
options: One policy defined once is attached consistently across every table that needs it, instead of reasoning about masking separately per table
Reusable functions run faster than any inline masking expression
A reusable function removes the need for any GRANT statements at all
Reusable functions can only be applied to exactly one table
questions.explain: Defining the mask once and attaching it with SET MASK across many tables keeps the policy consistent instead of duplicating logic per table.

questions.q: Why does generating GRANT statements from information_schema.tables matter at scale?
options: It avoids hand-typing hundreds of individual GRANT statements that would drift out of sync with what actually exists
information_schema.tables is the only way to create a table in Unity Catalog
It automatically deletes tables that don't yet have a GRANT
It replaces the need for any access control entirely
questions.explain: Scripting grants from the catalog's own metadata scales far better than hand-typing hundreds of GRANT statements one at a time.

questions.q: Why do SCIM-synced groups matter more at scale than individual grants?
options: Group membership changes from the identity provider propagate automatically, so grants attached to the group never need to be touched as people join or leave
SCIM sync is required before any GRANT statement can run at all
SCIM-synced groups remove the need for Unity Catalog entirely
Individual grants are always more secure than group-based grants
questions.explain: SCIM sync means access follows real identity-provider group membership automatically, without anyone editing GRANTs by hand.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what did Databricks & Delta Lake Lessons 42-43 already cover?
options: GRANT/REVOKE syntax and row/column security applied to a single table
Scripting grants across an entire schema from information_schema
SCIM-synced group membership from an identity provider
Auto Loader's file notification mode
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly recaps that single-table treatment before covering the patterns needed for hundreds of tables.

questions.q: What is the real problem with typing 300 individual GRANT statements by hand?
options: They inevitably drift out of sync with what tables actually exist over time
SQL does not allow more than 10 GRANT statements per session
Hand-typed GRANT statements execute more slowly than scripted ones
There is no real problem — it is the recommended production pattern
questions.explain: Manually maintained grant lists fall out of sync as new tables appear; scripting from metadata avoids that drift.
